ai-at-work.title: Anthropic is working on a system to prove AI models’ identity
ai-at-work.excerpt: Called FlashProve, the system would let anyone check that an AI response really came from the model it claims to be from.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Anthropic is building FlashProve, a verification system that lets you confirm an AI response actually came from the model claiming to produce it. This matters to digital workplace folks because AI is now embedded in your tools, and you need to know if you're getting answers from Claude or some sketchy knockoff pretending to be Claude. Honestly, it's about time someone tackled this, because right now you're basically taking AI outputs on faith, which is about as smart as accepting a resume without checking references.

ai-at-work.dwp_take: Ted Schlein's Ballistic Ventures is raising $490 million across two new funds to invest in AI-driven cybersecurity startups. This matters to digital workplace folks because security infrastructure directly impacts employee productivity, compliance requirements, and frankly, whether your organization gets ransomed on a Tuesday afternoon. Here's the thing: half a billion dollars chasing AI security solutions tells you the market is either genuinely terrified or genuinely onto something, and my money is on both being true.

ai-at-work.title: Sentra raises $150M to control what AI agents can reach in corporate data

ai-at-work.dwp_take: Sentra just pulled in $150 million to build guardrails around what AI agents can access in your corporate data vaults, riding massive 300% growth over the past year. Here's the thing though: if companies actually needed to raise $150 million to figure out data access control, we've been doing security wrong for decades, and this is just expensive duct tape on a broken process.

Look, I've seen plenty of "AI will replace your job" hype, but automating the repetitive pages at 3am? That part might actually stick.

tools-tech.title: SUSE lays off 1 in 10 workers – citing AI and automation
tools-tech.excerpt: Squarespace also announced layoffs this week, but explicit ties to AI remain inconsistent.
tools-tech.dwp_take: SUSE announced layoffs affecting 10 percent of its workforce, explicitly blaming AI and automation for the reduction. For digital workplace pros, this signals that enterprise software vendors are serious about restructuring around AI capabilities, which means your tools and platforms will shift faster than you'd expect. Here's the thing though: every company laying people off suddenly claims it's because of AI, when really it's usually just the same old cost-cutting dressed up in shinier language.

tools-tech.title: Windows 11 can run better on PCs with 8GB now, Microsoft says – here’s why
tools-tech.excerpt: The latest updates to Windows 11 offer improvements in speed, performance, and memory management.
tools-tech.dwp_take: Microsoft finally admitted that 8GB of RAM is adequate for Windows 11 and released updates to prove it. This matters because plenty of organizations are still running older hardware, and knowing they can upgrade to Windows 11 without replacing entire fleets changes the calculus on modernization timelines and budgets. Honestly, it's refreshing to see Microsoft acknowledge reality instead of pushing everyone toward 16GB machines, though I'd still recommend 16GB for anyone doing real work rather than just existing on their PC.

tools-tech.dwp_take: Tech companies are laying off workers in 2026 despite strong profits, blaming AI automation and workforce reconfiguration for the cuts. Digital workplace pros need to understand this trend because they'll be managing the messaging, culture, and infrastructure fallout when headcount decisions hit their own organizations. Here's the thing: when companies cut people to boost margins rather than survive downturns, your job just became part crisis management and part damage control, which wasn't in your job description but definitely will be on your plate.

tools-tech.title: Get a load of Excel’s new multi-value cells
tools-tech.excerpt: Until now, Microsoft Excel has followed a strict structural rule: each cell on a worksheet can hold only a single scalar value. While you can string together text using commas or write dynamic array f
tools-tech.dwp_take: Microsoft is letting Excel cells hold multiple values at once instead of forcing users to wrangle data across separate cells or use workarounds like dynamic arrays. This matters to workplace pros because spreadsheets are still how most organizations actually get work done, and better data structure means less time spent reformatting and more time spent on actual analysis. After thirty years watching Excel users bend spreadsheets into pretzels to do basic tasks, I'm cautiously optimistic that Microsoft finally realized making the software less annoying might be worth their time.

digital-culture.title: Why taste, conviction, foresight, and courage are the traits we need in the age of AI
digital-culture.excerpt: Many call the development of artificial intelligence the Fourth Industrial Revolution, but I disagree. I would say AI is the first, and the last, intelligence revolution. Every industrial revolution m
digital-culture.dwp_take: Someone at Fast Company argues that AI represents a unique intelligence revolution because it's making cognition itself cheap, unlike previous revolutions that just made physical resources cheaper. This matters to digital workplace pros because we're about to manage teams where thinking work gets radically commodified, forcing us to figure out what humans actually do better. Here's the thing: if cognition becomes cheap, your organization's taste and conviction become your actual competitive advantage, which means you'd better know what you stand for beyond "we use AI now."

digital-culture.title: Am I going to be fired by AI? How corporate America is being seduced by AI and algorithms in the ‘forever layoffs’ era
digital-culture.excerpt: For five years, the former Meta employee had been feted as a high performer by her managers. She had even received a rare equity award in recognition of her performance, which had never fallen below a
digital-culture.dwp_take: A high-performing Meta employee with consistent top ratings and equity awards got laid off anyway, part of the wave of AI-driven workforce reductions hitting corporate America. Digital workplace leaders need to understand that algorithmic layoffs bypass traditional performance metrics, meaning your internal communications strategy and career development programs might be talking to ghosts. Here's the uncomfortable truth: if your company is using AI to make headcount decisions, no amount of "exceeds expectations" ratings will save you, which is exactly why employees are losing faith in annual reviews faster than companies are adopting ChatGPT.

digital-culture.title: Workforce data, smarter AI integration among greatest workplace priorities in the new year
digital-culture.excerpt: The importance of workforce data is just one of the prognostications people managers are making looking to the year ahead.
digital-culture.dwp_take: Companies are betting that better workforce data and smarter AI integration will be their top workplace priorities in 2025. This matters because digital workplace leaders need to actually know what data they're collecting, where it lives, and whether their AI tools are solving real problems or just creating new ones. Here's the thing though: I've watched organizations chase data and AI priorities for years, and the ones that actually win are the ones who start by asking "what question are we trying to answer" instead of "what shiny tool can we buy."
